newsitem.title: USA: Jury sworn-in for Michael Jackson trial.
newsitem.headline: Jury sworn-in for Michael Jackson trial.

text.p: A jury was sworn in on Tuesday for the trial of a wrongful termination suit filed against pop star Michael Jackson by five former employees of his Neverland ranch.

Opening arguments were scheduled to begin on Wednesday after a two-man, 10-woman jury and four alternates were chosen in Santa Barbara County Court in Santa Maria, 125 miles (200 km) north of Los Angeles.

Three of Jackson's former bodyguards, a maid and an administrative assistant sued Jackson and six of his aides, alleging they installed recording devices at his ranch to find out what they knew about molestation allegations against him. The plaintiffs say they were forced out of their jobs.

In 1993 a 13-year-old boy said Jackson molested him. The boy sued Jackson but the lawsuit was settled out of court for a reported $15 million. Jackson, who has denied any wrongdoing, was never charged with a crime.
Judge Zel Canter told prospective jurors on Tuesday to put aside Jackson's role as an entertainer and view the so-called "King of Pop" as merely an employer for the purposes of the case.
One woman on the jury told the judge she did not like the idea of serving on a child-molestation case, but Canter told her that was not the primary issue of the case.

An older man was asked by the judge if he liked Jackson's music. He replied: "I don't like Michael Jackson music, I don't listen to it and I don't think the guy can dance." Canter kept him on the panel anyway.
The judge has denied media requests to televise or tape-record the trial, saying he wanted to protect the privacy of witnesses.

It was not known whether Jackson will testify in person at the trial. Lawyers for the former employees have subpoenaed him, but because he is not a full-time resident of California, doubts have been raised over whether the subpoena can be enforced.
The ex-employees filed suit in February last year, alleging they were forced to resign from the Neverland Ranch in July 1994. They have not specified the amount of financial damages they are seeking.
Jackson's attorney, Robert Sanger, said last week that the ex-employees "just walked off the job and got together and made these allegations."

In a related development, Jackson's estranged wife Lisa Marie Presley filed a motion in the same court on Tuesday seeking to see details of the private settlement Jackson reached with the boy who accused him of molestation.
The boy's father has sued Jackson and Presley, alleging they violated the terms of the settlement when they gave an interview on ABC television.
Presley's lawyers will be in court on Thursday to argue their client has no knowledge of the details of the settlement.
